title: Settle evaluation contracts before scanner flywheel
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want the corpus and fixture harness contracts settled in writing, so that later scanner work is steered by honest scores instead of alias tricks, unread files counted as misses, or two scorers that disagree.

This epic is for **design**, not for retuning detectors, adding PHP/Ruby ingest, or renaming Checkr. Those are scanner problems. We do not start using the evaluation system to improve the scanner until the questions on the child tasks have answers that code, gold YAML, and docs all implement.

## Why this exists

We imported 29 packets of gold into `DataParade-io/scanner` so a public `dataparade-cli` release could not wipe them. The corpus runner can produce per-layer numbers. Those numbers are still not a safe flywheel:

- Gold taxonomy keys (`pii:email_address`) and matcher rule ids (`mention:email`, `data_item:ssn`) are bridged by `tests/eval/identity.ts` aliases.
- Unread evidence can still enter recall if it appears on an exhaustive-scope list.
- `tests/eval/score.ts` and `tests/benchmark/precision.ts` do not implement the same match rules.
- Jest is five grades; corpus gold is four layers (`pii_signals` loaded as `mentions`, no `raw_hits` packets).
- Component and flow gold uses exact `type:name` keys, so vendor naming misses look like total recall failure.
- There is no frozen baseline of **evaluable (read) only** scores.

Child tasks are one issue each. Deep-thinking agents should argue the contract, propose a single decision, and list what must change in scorer, adapters, gold, and docs. They must not “fix” the scanner to make today’s messy scores look better.

## Out of scope

- Language ingest (PHP, Ruby, Swift, Rust) except as it affects the unread rule.
- Component naming quality (`third_party:checkr` vs `asset:requests call`) except as a documentedGap / naming-grade policy.
- Leftover proposed original-ten gold (incomplete corpus, not a harness contract).
- Making Plexus GraphQL eval run (a second client; align it after the scanner harness is the source of truth).

## Definition of done

Each child task has a recorded decision (and rejected alternatives). Follow-on implementation work is separate tasks. This epic closes when all six design questions are answered and the answers do not contradict each other.

comments.text:
Child design tasks (one question each, for multi-agent deep thinking — no scanner retune until decided):

1. KDATAP-d6eabf — One identity vocabulary for gold, adapters, and docs
2. KDATAP-791091 — Unread means ingest never opened the file
3. KDATAP-89d1a6 — One scorer for all headline metrics
4. KDATAP-f6b6e7 — One layer model for Jest and corpus
5. KDATAP-08a0ac — Policy for component and flow identity
6. KDATAP-955d82 — Frozen evaluable-only corpus baseline

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Agreed evaluation-contract direction

Stakeholder discussion resolved the six design questions with one overarching rule: semantic normalization, eligibility, matching, and reporting are separate contracts and none may silently repair another.

The agreed architecture is:

1. Both gold and scanner findings map into a versioned canonical evaluation representation. Identity, classification, instance/vendor, evidence, and display names are separate. Broad aliases, labels-as-identity, and display-name matching are removed.
2. Eligibility is per layer and per canonical evidence path, with reasoned coverage outcomes. Exhaustive scope cannot make evidence readable.
3. One canonical evaluator performs deterministic one-to-one matching and owns recall, classification/label metrics, precision, negatives, unread, and unscorable reporting.
4. The headline product is a four-layer scorecard: mentions, repository-level data items, components, and data flows. Raw hits are diagnostic. No heterogeneous overall scalar is published.
5. Components and flows use structured taxonomy and graph identities, with a strict result plus diagnostic attribution. Partial detection does not become strict success, and locationless findings do not silently disappear.
6. Baselines are immutable contract-versioned artifacts with complete scanner, corpus, taxonomy, adapter, dependency, and source-SHA fingerprints. Contract changes receive bridge runs; detector changes never overwrite the reference baseline.

Two previously implicit requirements are now explicit:

- the unit and cardinality of an observation must be defined for every layer, because the current data-item collapse plus identity-only any-match scoring lets one finding satisfy multiple accepted gold cases;
- closed-world scope belongs to packet-and-layer review metadata, not only to positive annotations, so zero-positive reviewed scopes can measure false positives.

Rejected system-level alternatives are matcher vocabulary as truth, current gold strings as an unversioned contract, fuzzy equivalence groups, shared global read coverage, multiple scorers, five duplicated headline layers, opaque graph string aliases, and mutable incomparable baselines.

These comments settle design. Follow-on implementation work must be filed separately and should cover the canonical schema and migration, adapter/taxonomy maps, per-layer eligibility ledger, scope migration, one-to-one evaluator, four-layer runner, structured graph model, client de-duplication, and reproducible baseline artifacts. Scanner retuning and new language ingest remain outside this epic and must not begin from current scores.
